intro: “Ranjish Hi Sahi” is a deeply emotional Urdu ghazal written by Ahmad Faraz and made famous by Mehdi Hassan. The song captures the anguish of unrequited love and longing, where the singer pleads for their beloved to return, even if only to hurt them again. It reflects themes of pain, estrangement, and the paradox of love, where even suffering in love is preferable to complete abandonment.

deva: रंजिश ही सही दिल ही दुखाने के लिए आ
आ फिर से मुझे छोड़ के जाने के लिए आ

en: Let it be anguish, even to torment my heart, come,
Come once again, even if only to abandon me.

deva: कुछ तो मिरे पिंदार-ए-मोहब्बत का भरम रख
तू भी तो कभी मुझ को मनाने के लिए आ

en: Respect, if only a little, the pride of my love for you,
Come, someday, to console me as well.

gloss.meaning: the pride, the self-regard, of love

deva: पहले से मरासिम न सही फिर भी कभी तो
रस्म-ओ-रह-ए-दुनिया ही निभाने के लिए आ

en: If not for past affections, then at least for the sake of propriety,
Come, if only to honor the customs of this world.

gloss.meaning: the customs and ways of the world

deva: किस किस को बताएँगे जुदाई का सबब हम
तू मुझ से ख़फ़ा है तो ज़माने के लिए आ

en: How many people will I explain my sorrow to?
If you are mad at me, then come, if only for the world’s sake.

deva: इक उम्र से हूँ लज़्ज़त-ए-गिर्या से भी महरूम
ऐ राहत-ए-जाँ मुझ को रुलाने के लिए आ

en: For ages, I have been deprived of the solace of tears,
O peace of my soul, come back, if only to make me weep.

gloss.meaning: comfort of my life: the beloved

deva: अब तक दिल-ए-ख़ुश-फ़ह्‌म को तुझ से हैं उमीदें
ये आख़िरी शम'एँ भी बुझाने के लिए आ

en: Till now, my naive heart still holds some hope in you,
Come, and snuff out even these last flickering candles of expectation.

gloss.meaning: a heart that believes what it hopes

added.textNote: Sung by Mehdi Hassan. Not in the published text.

en: Agreed, concealing love is the true essence of love,
But one day, come secretly, to confess it in silence.

added.textNote: Sung by Mehdi Hassan. Not in the published text.

en: Just as you have excuses for never arriving,
Someday, make an excuse to never leave.

addedIntro: Mehdi Hassan sings two further couplets as part of this ghazal. They are not in Faraz’s text as published on Rekhta; one source attributes them to the poet Talib Baghpati. They are kept apart here rather than credited to Faraz.
